question: What is the main goal of a nursing audit?

options.A: To evaluate and improve the quality of patient care
options.B: To punish nurses who make mistakes in documentation
options.C: To determine the monthly salary of nursing staff
options.D: To count the total number of hospital bed sheets

explanation: You've got this! Audits aren't witch hunts—they are helpful tools to check our care against set standards so we can find ways to do even better for our patients. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h1)

question: How is a nursing audit different from a general staff performance appraisal?

options.A: Audits are done only by doctors, while appraisals are done by senior nurses
options.B: Audits deal with hospital finances, while appraisals deal with patient beds
options.C: Audits happen daily, while appraisals happen only once in a lifetime
options.D: Audits focus on patient care processes, while appraisals focus on overall staff conduct

explanation: Great thinking! A performance appraisal looks at how a nurse behaves on the job overall, while an audit zooms in specifically on clinical care and nursing records. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why are nursing audits so important for quality assurance?

options.A: They reduce the cost of purchasing hospital medications
options.B: They help discover gaps between standard care and actual practice
options.C: They guarantee that patients will never experience complications
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for physician supervision

explanation: Spot on! By comparing what we actually do against established guidelines, audits show us clearly where our care needs a little extra boost. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h2)

question: A hospital management wants to check if nurses are keeping proper wound care records. What should they do?

options.A: Increasing the number of night shifts for junior nurses
options.B: Transferring patients with wounds to a different facility
options.C: Organizing a social party for all the nursing staff
options.D: Conducting a nursing audit of surgical ward case notes

explanation: Exactly! Reviewing actual clinical charts through an audit gives clear proof of how well wound care is being documented and performed. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h2)

question: When is a retrospective nursing audit done?

options.A: After the patient has been discharged from the hospital
options.B: While the patient is actively receiving treatment on the ward
options.C: Before the patient is even admitted to the emergency room
options.D: During the exact moment a surgical operation is happening

explanation: You got it! Think of 'retrospective' as looking backward—these audits review completed medical records after the patient has already left the facility. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the big advantage of a concurrent audit compared to a retrospective one?

options.A: It requires zero paperwork or review of patient case notes
options.B: Errors can be corrected immediately while the patient is still admitted
options.C: It takes much longer to complete and involves more paperwork
options.D: It is only performed by the hospital director or chief medical officer

explanation: Brilliant! Because concurrent audits happen in real-time, we can catch missing care and fix documentation right away before the patient goes home. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the very first step when planning a nursing audit?

options.A: Buying new computers for the nursing office
options.B: Establishing criteria and standards of care
options.C: Punishing nurses who fail to write reports
options.D: Discharging all patients from the medical ward

explanation: Makes total sense! We have to decide what excellent care looks like first before we can measure our actual work against it. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why do we carry out a re-audit near the end of a quality improvement cycle?

options.A: To find new reasons to query junior nursing staff members
options.B: To see if the corrective actions successfully improved care
options.C: To comply with international travel laws for nurses
options.D: To increase the amount of paperwork stored in the archive

explanation: Spot on! A re-audit helps us check whether the changes we put in place actually solved the problems we found during our first check. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h4)

question: What primary tool do auditors use to collect data during a nursing audit?

options.A: Surgical scalpels and sterile dressing forceps
options.B: Microscopes and laboratory blood testing kits
options.C: Stethoscopes and digital blood pressure cuffs
options.D: Structured checklists and patient case notes

explanation: You're doing great! Auditors dive into written patient records and charts using structured checklists to measure care against set standards. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is a major risk when relying only on written charts during an audit?

options.A: Patients will refuse to take their prescribed hospital medications
options.B: Doctors will take over all the responsibilities of the nursing staff
options.C: Care might have been given but simply not documented by the nurse
options.D: Case notes might turn into digital files without any human input

explanation: Exactly! Heavy workloads on the ward sometimes mean a nurse performed a procedure wonderfully, but was simply too busy to write it down. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h5)

question: How are audit findings usually summarized when presenting to management?

options.B: In long, unedited hand-written story books
options.C: Through musical drama performances on the ward
options.D: By listing the personal secrets of every staff nurse

explanation: Correct! Data is usually bundled into clear numbers and percentages so everyone can easily see our compliance rates at a glance. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why is it so important to find the root cause of a gap found during an audit?

options.A: To justify closing down the nursing department permanently
options.B: To make sure every single nurse on duty receives a formal warning
options.C: So the corrective action actually fixes the real underlying problem
options.D: To prove that the hospital administration has zero funds left

explanation: You nailed it! Finding the root cause ensures we fix the actual issue—whether it's a lack of training or a shortage of supplies—rather than just guessing. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h6)

question: What should happen immediately after identifying gaps in a nursing audit?

options.A: Destroying all patient records to protect staff privacy
options.B: Stopping all patient admissions to the hospital
options.C: Implementing corrective actions to improve the care
options.D: Firing all nursing supervisors on the affected ward

explanation: That's right! Audits are meant to spark positive change, so we must put practical solutions in place right away to fix what was broken. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h7)

question: An audit shows nurses forget pain scores because the chart has no space for them. What is the best fix?

options.A: Suspending every nurse working on the ward without pay
options.B: Banning the use of all written documents on the hospital ward
options.C: Telling patients they must diagnose their own pain levels
options.D: Redesigning the pain chart to include a clear, dedicated space for scores

explanation: Smart thinking! Fixing the document layout makes proper charting much easier for busy nurses, solving the root cause of the missing data. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to nursing audits in many Nigerian healthcare facilities?

options.A: Severe shortage of nursing staff and high workloads
options.B: Fear of victimization among junior nursing staff
options.C: Excessive availability of fully automated robotic wards
options.D: Heavy reliance on physical, paper-based case notes

explanation: You got it! Fully automated robotic wards are definitely not common hurdles here. Instead, staff shortages, paper files, and fear of query are our real daily challenges. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h8)

question: Why does a high patient-to-nurse ratio make nursing audits difficult?

options.A: Nurses are too overwhelmed with direct patient care to conduct or participate in audits
options.B: Paper case notes will disappear from the wards every single night
options.C: Patients will refuse to let doctors check their vital signs
options.D: Hospitals will automatically close down all nursing schools

explanation: Spot on! When nurses are stretched thin caring for too many patients at once, finding extra time for chart reviews and quality improvement is tough. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h8)
